Question: What are some things people often do that contribute to climate change?
Answer: Caution, this will be a frustrating answer. Almost everything. 200 years ago, a tiny fraction of the public could afford the massive transportation costs. Most people ate things that were in season within 10 miles of their home. Most people wore what was available in general vicinity. And most homes were made of materials available locally. When we lived in a podunk town in India, the only vegetables that were available were what were in season. Tomatoes went from 0.25 rupees a kilogram to 5 rupees a kilo depending on the season. That is a swing of 20x. Mangoes would come in season and would be plentiful and then disappear and no matter how much money you had, you couldn’t get a mango till the next season. Same thing with clothes. Same thing with construction materials. Today, I live in a house with a kitchen with granite countertops from China, cabinets from New Jersey and floor tiles from Italy. I have carpets from India, TV from South Korea, glasses from Germany, Austria and many other countries. My wife and I eat avocados every week all year round without even thinking where they are from. If we want to make a serious dent in our carbon footprint, we would have to consume less. And not many of us are ready to do that. We all want big houses, big cars, big meals, big closets full of clothes in all styles, shapes and colors and we want everything cheap. Most Americans are not even comfortable being bound by the schedule of the local public transit.
